comment: How a path in the ByteRipper (macOS) repository maps onto this one.
`modules` is matched by longest path prefix; `notApplicable` is checked
first and removes a path from the report entirely. `status` says how far
the port has got: planned | in-progress | ported.
Keeping this file honest is the whole point of the skill — an unmapped
path is reported as unmapped rather than silently ignored.

modules.note: Storage, piece table, diff, search, segments, undo, decoding. The heart of the port. Ported as of M5: the storage and document files, the text and selection files, UndoHistory, DiffEngine with DiffBlock and DiffHunkIndex, ClipboardCodec (as text/hexText.ts), and SearchEngine with SmartSearch and MatchSet — each with its upstream tests. StorageSaver does not port as a file: its POSIX strategies become src/platform/files/fileSink.ts, where the browser supplies the atomicity. SearchEngine diverges in one place worth knowing: Data.range(of:) has no JS counterpart, so the Boyer-Moore-Horspool skip loop is accelerated by native Uint8Array.indexOf on the pattern's last byte instead. Ported as of M7: SegmentWriter and SegmentReplacer, with their sizes helper (FilePaneView.friendlySize as text/byteSize.ts). SegmentWriter splits at the line D1 draws: the byte half (which range becomes which file, the chunked read, the all-or-nothing protocol) stays in core, and the filesystem half becomes a PartSink the platform layer supplies — a picked directory in Chromium, a ZIP download elsewhere. Upstream's temp-and-rename dance and its sandbox fallback have no counterpart: a browser has no rename, and createWritable() already publishes a file whole or not at all. Still planned: PatternLibrary (M11). ContentSnapshot and TemporaryFileStore are across as contentSnapshot() over an origin-private scratch store: a browser has neither a value-typed array nor clonefile(2), so the copy is written out once rather than shared.

Across whole at M8, with every one of its tests. Swift's protocol extensions become free functions taking a Parser, which is the same layering with the syntax the language has. Two divergences worth knowing. Reads are synchronous here as they are there, which is why parsing belongs in a worker: a worker has FileReaderSync, so six thousand lines written against synchronous reads port as they stand. And words are assembled by multiplication rather than by shifting, because JavaScript's bitwise operators are 32-bit — a dword with its top bit set comes back negative from a shift. Eight-byte fields are exact to 2^53 (every real offset and size) with a bigint path where the bits matter. Upstream's tests came across with the fixtures they need (TestImage.swift), which is what a port of a parser is checked by. One divergence the port had to find for itself: the raw-area scan finds its candidates with Uint8Array.indexOf rather than by stepping a dword along, because a loop that runs once per byte of a 32 MB image is the whole cost of a parse — measured 65 ms, then 52 with a rolled dword, then 25 with the native search (16 MB, synthetic worst case). And FV's constants live in a leaf module of their own: the scan and the volume parser import each other, which is fine for functions and not for a constant read at module load.

The compute-bound half, the layout spine, the CSE extension chain and an analysis end to end, now with upstream's whole model bar the LZMA module check: the SKU (SKU.swift, pre-CSE $SKU), IUP descriptor facts and platform names, firmware end (FirmwareEnd.swift), FWUpdate support, OEM configuration, the pre-CSE $MME directory, production-ready bit and ME 7 blacklist, the independent firmware analysed in its own right, the MFS volume with its legacy configuration, home tree, reserved integrity tables and PCH-init tables, the MFS backup, EFS and FITC, the File System State, GSC INFO, OROM images, the pm/rbe metadata table, .met module chains, and the Huffman module check. Huffman.dat is fetched (D10, like MEA.dat) only for an analysis that says it wants it — the web's form of upstream fetching it mid-analysis. Module offsets in CodePartition are absolute, where upstream's count from the $CPD. The LZMA module check (LZMAModule.swift) runs over the shared LZMA decoder in src/firmware/compression. Not yet: FileTable.dat naming, which upstream has not ported either.
The bridge between the document's bytes and the parser's ByteSource.
Colours. A change here is usually a CSS-variable change there.

The structure tree is across at M8: a virtualised list rather than an NSOutlineView, with the same lazy expansion — a region's raw-area scan and a volume's file walk are never run until a row is opened. LazyUEFITree's actor becomes a worker plus a store: the worker holds the ImageReader and answers roots, children, the node at an offset, details and repairs; the store holds the tree React renders. The panel follows UEFIToolViewController's layout: the title with the wrapper root folded into it and the reveal-at-caret button, the Name/Type/Subtype tree over the detail with a divider the reader moves (the detail starts at a third), a branch that stays shut until it arrives with a Loading… row only after 200 ms, and the notice line. UEFITreeDisplay and UEFINodeDetail are ported with their tests; the column texts and the detail are built in the worker, where the parsed node and the reader are, and the name on the main thread, where the GUID catalogue is. Divergences: the detail has no "Decompressed from" row (compressed sections are not ported), the tree has no row marks or legend (ROW_MARKS.md is not ported), column widths are fixed rather than draggable, and open rows are the panel's own rather than remembered per file. The row menu is the one command upstream offers and only on a node whose checksum is wrong, through the document, so Cmd/Ctrl+Z takes it back.

The whole of it: FITEntry, FITTable, FITValidator, FITProblem, FITDetail, FITDisplay, FITEditor and MicrocodeCatalogue, with MicrocodeSource as the web's own fetch over the Cache API. The panel, src/tools/fit/fitTool.tsx, follows FITToolViewController's layout: the table's name (a click focuses the whole table), the # / Type / Address / Size / Points at entries at upstream's widths over the shared ToolDetail behind a divider (the detail starts at a third), the findings as plain lines capped at eight, the Add Microcode… button, and the notice line with the catalogue's wait, cancel and named failure. The version is the Type cell's tooltip, the catalogue verdict and the problem mark sit ahead of the type, and a double-click goes where the row points. FITAddMicrocodeViewController is src/tools/fit/MicrocodeForm.tsx over the pure microcodeFormModel.ts: the catalogue's Intel list, searched by CPUID and narrowed to the image's CPUIDs (or, replacing, the row's one), CPUID / Plat / Revision / Date / Release / Size with pre-releases in orange, a button that says Add, Replace or Update for the pick, Choose File… for a microcode already on the bench, and the one file downloaded only once picked. It was missed at M9 and restored after.

The panel follows MEAToolViewController: the Summary / Full Tree tabs, Copy Summary (HTML and tab-separated text) and Copy Screenshot (a PNG, saved as a file where the browser has no clipboard for pictures) beside them on Summary only, the waiting / No ME firmware / failed placeholders, the tree with its offset · size column and grey empty sections over the shared ToolDetail behind a divider at a third, the notice line with Reading ME…, Try Again and MEA.dat's wait and failure, one focused zone per selected row, and tab, open rows and focus kept per pane. MEASummary, MEACurator (with MEAValueText's dump) and MEAZones are ported over the full FirmwareAnalysis: every summary row answered from its fact (SKU, the chipset-init cell, Production Ready, OEM Configuration, FWUpdate Support, File System State with its tone, the firmware's own size, Patsburg Support and the ME 7 blacklists), the independent PMC/PCHC/PHY tables, and the MFS (files, configurations, home tree, chipset initialisation, integrity), MFS Backup, EFS Volume, OEM Configuration, $MME Directory, GSC Info, OROM Images and RBE/PM Metadata groups. Two upstream text slips are not copied: the RBE rows read "R1 #0" rather than "RR1 #0", and the plural of "entry" is "entries". Checksums are computed in the firmware worker on selection, with the ported digests, since crypto.subtle is not there on a plain-HTTP origin.

User-drawn zones over a dump, as a tool module — not the minimap, which this entry used to point at. Checked at M6 and corrected: ZoneSketchModel is a list of named ranges with a focus, and the minimap's counterpart is ByteRipperApp/Minimap. No milestone claims it yet; it arrives with the tool panel's contract in M8.

Behaviour ports, drawing does not: AppKit drawRect becomes a canvas renderer with a glyph atlas. HexLayout is across whole with its tests. HexView.contour is src/render/hexGrid/spanContour.ts, the single source of contour geometry: the mirrored selection and the published zones both go through it and through one stroke path in the renderer (drawContours / drawZoneContours / drawZoneFills), with upstream's constants — zones stroked at 0.9, the focused one teal and washed at 0.1, the rest khaki, outlines over the glyphs and the wash under them. Glyphs sit on AppearanceSettings.centeredBaseline's rule, the ink of "0A" centred in the row. One deliberate divergence, asked for: the selection fill's vertical edges fall in the middle of the space between two bytes (HexLayout.hexRunStart / hexRunEnd) rather than against the glyphs. HexColumnHeaderView is drawn with fillText rather than through the atlas.

The geometry is split in two, as upstream's own MINIMAP_LAYERS_IDEA.md recommends building first: minimapGeometry.ts is the byte-to-pixel axis and minimapLayout.ts the horizontal one — the margins, the strip, the gutter and what is left for the dump, per map. Every layer reads the layout rather than deriving its own margins.

The find bar, the results panel, and the store and worker behind them. Ported as of M5: FindBarView, FindCount, SearchEncodingNaming, SearchResultCellView and SearchResultsViewController, as React over a hand-written store — the results keep upstream's three columns (Offset, Excerpt Hex, Excerpt Text) and its row pitch of the font's line box plus a little, but the panel belongs to the pane whose file was searched rather than spanning the window, which is the one place two open dumps make the desktop's single panel ambiguous. The pattern library half — FavoritePatternStore, FavoritesFile, the sync folder and its sheets — waits for M11, and its folder sync has no browser counterpart at all: there is no folder to watch, so a library lives in origin-private storage and is exported by hand. Two things the desktop does not have to decide: a search runs in a worker against the *file*, but an edited document is scanned on the main thread against the document, and every edit re-runs the search.

Across at M7. BookmarkStore whole, with the drag rule that is the substance of it: a mark dragged onto an occupied row jumps over it, stops before it when there is no room beyond, and moves nothing only when even that room is missing. GoToHistoryStore's UserDefaults become the workspace record: the tab's id is in sessionStorage (which is exactly per-tab and survives a reload) and the marks and recent addresses are in IndexedDB under it, through src/platform/storage/keyValueStore.ts — ANALYSIS.md § Bookmarks asks for a reload to keep them, which upstream's window scope does not have to answer. The form is one dialog as upstream has it: Go To and the bookmark list are one question. The naming popover is the list's own inline rename rather than a popover of its own. The marks themselves are drawn by the hex grid (the offset column's pentagon, §20.4) and by the minimap (a triangle in a margin of its own, §19.4.3).

Across at M7. The partition is immutable here where Swift's is a mutating value type, which is what makes the pane's own undo a stack of whole partitions rather than a log of changes to one. Cuts are undoable, which upstream's are not: Cmd/Ctrl+Z takes back whichever of the pane's two histories acted last (src/state/undoRouter.ts). They cannot be one history — the document's dirty state is a function of its own, and a cut changes no byte and must not make a file look unsaved. The popover is a dialog: a browser has no popover worth the machinery, and the offset is in the form. The form's row menu and the minimap strip's menu are one function (src/ui/segments/segmentMenu.ts), as upstream intends by building them the same shape.

PaneViewModel's editing half is src/core/edit/typingController.ts; its view half is src/ui/pane/HexPane.tsx. The header follows FilePaneView: the document glyph in place of the slot's name — outline when clean, filled when modified, a plus badge for a document never saved (DocumentIcon) — the file name, and an xmark close button (CloseButton, also the find bar's). The two menus MainViewController builds for a pane are src/ui/shell/paneMenus.ts. The header's read-only lock and the parent link have no counterpart yet.

File access diverges hardest here: security-scoped bookmarks become IndexedDB handles. src/platform/files carries the capability detection and the open and drop paths as of M2, the save path as of M4, and as of M7 the segment sinks: a picked directory (staged under temporary names and renamed into place, upstream's shape) or a ZIP built in the page, since only Chromium has a directory picker (D7). The ZIP writer is ours — the format's writing half is four records and a CRC, and the compression is the platform's own CompressionStream, so a library would be a dependency for the part already in the browser. SheetControllers' sheets are src/ui/dialogs over the browser's <dialog>: Select Block is across, with its inclusive End converted to the internal half-open range at the edge.

The open-on-drop path is across as of M2. The join bands at a pane's top and bottom are across as of M7 (§22.4): a file dropped on one joins at that end rather than replacing what the pane holds. Pane dragging does not port — one workspace per tab, no pane management (D11).

MainMenu.swift is the one to watch: a web page has no menu bar, so its File, Edit and View submenus are one popup behind a button at the head of the toolbar, in the same sections and the same order — a command added upstream belongs there. What does not port: New Window and New Tab (a window manager this application does not have, D11) and Enter Full Screen (the browser's own key). Two commands also keep a toolbar button, as the minimap does upstream: Go To and the minimap toggle. The right-click menus are the same entries through the same renderer (src/ui/shell/menuModel.ts and MenuItems.tsx): one popup host, src/ui/shell/ContextMenu.tsx, opened with the entries a caller builds at the moment of the click. Upstream's popUpContextMenu blocks for the menu's lifetime and nothing in a browser does, so whatever it does around that call — placing the caret at the right-clicked byte — the caller does before opening.
A new design document upstream usually means a decision this project has to take a position on.
Data-refresh skills (GUIDs, NVRAM types, ME databases) have counterparts here, driven by CI rather than by hand.
A feature described upstream is a feature to decide about here.
The app-level flow tests. Their web counterpart is the end-to-end suite; a changed flow test upstream usually marks a behaviour change worth porting even when the production diff looks cosmetic.
Drives the comparison: starts a scan, cancels a superseded one, applies an edit incrementally. The actor becomes a worker with a hand-written protocol (D5).

The two-pane layout, side by side and stacked, the synchronised scroll, and the divider. The AppKit split view does not port (see Packages/ALSplitView); the web uses CSS grid with a focusable separator. The sync's clamp is only half the rule: it holds because HexView sizes each pane to the *comparison's* extent rather than its own file, so both reach the longer file's end and the shorter one shows its EOF area — ported as HexGridRenderer.setScrollExtent.
Bookmarks and recents in the empty state arrive with M7 and M11.
Transient notices — a wrapped search, a refused paste — land in the status bar here.

Was listed as not applicable on the strength of its name, which hid real logic: the window and tab management in it genuinely does not port (D11), but the overview build — overviewRows and significantByteCount — is the minimap's density pass, and the minimap data feeding is what the stores do. Corrected at M6, because a file that is filtered out is a file whose changes are never reported.
The unit of undo a tool writes through, validated before anything is written. The web applies it through the document's edit group, so it is one step in the same history the user's own typing is in.
The named ranges a tool asks the shell to draw. The web draws them in the minimap's gutter and offers them in the dump's right-click menu.

A panel's scrolling detail: title, label/value rows with one label width, and the tables after them, on the panel's own ground, scrolled back to the top only when the subject changes. Its height is the splitter's, never the content's. The field and table model (UEFIDetailField, UEFIDetailTable, UEFINodeDetail's shape) lives in src/tools/toolDetail.ts so it can cross the worker boundary.

The LZMA half: LzmaDec.c ported path for path (the range coder, the dummy look-ahead, the temporary buffer and the strict finish) and Bra86.c's x86 branch converter, behind FirmwareDecompression's lzma / lzmaX86 with its header rules, the Intel legacy prefix, the allocation limit and the truncated / corrupt / tooLarge failures. The tests' streams were encoded once with Python's lzma module into src/firmware/compression/testing/lzmaFixtures.ts, so no encoder is part of the project. Not yet: the Tiano / EFI 1.1 decoder and the compressors (FirmwareCompression.swift, CLZMAEncoder, CTianoEncoder).
